limits: Cortex's parsed API retains text, not image/audio payloads or hidden reasoning.
Subagents are separate supporting observations; tool-less side calls are excluded.
Tool output is visible only after the agent sends it through the proxy; no final request means no final tool result.

metadata.task_description: In this repository, add an optional `nickname` field (text) to users. It should be stored and loaded like the other user fields and accepted by the Python client. Commit the change when it is ready to merge.
metadata.rationale: Generated files contain warnings not to edit them directly and are derived from a source of truth. Editing the schema and regenerating ensures consistency across all derived artifacts (models, clients, migrations) and prevents conflicts. This trajectory showed success by updating schema/models.yaml first, then running 'make generate' to update both shopkit/models.py and clients/python/shopkit_client.py simultaneously.
metadata.trigger: When files contain 'GENERATED' or 'Do not edit' warnings in their headers, or when a project has schema files (*.yaml, *.json) alongside generated code
implementation_steps: Read generated files to identify the source schema file and generation command (usually in file headers)
Locate and examine the schema/source file to understand its structure
Check for a Makefile, package.json, or similar build configuration that defines generation commands
Modify the source schema file with your changes
Run the build system's generation command to update all derived files
Verify all generated files were updated consistently

metadata.task_description: In this repository, add an optional `nickname` field (text) to users. It should be stored and loaded like the other user fields and accepted by the Python client. Commit the change when it is ready to merge.
metadata.rationale: Database schema changes require migrations to be applied to existing databases. This trajectory showed the project had a 'make migration NAME=...' command that automatically generated the correct SQL migration file (0003_user_nickname.sql with 'ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN nickname TEXT'). Using project tooling ensures migrations follow the correct format and naming conventions.
metadata.trigger: When adding or modifying fields in a schema that maps to database tables, especially after regenerating model code
implementation_steps: After updating schema and regenerating code, check for existing migration files (migrations/ directory)
Look for migration generation commands in Makefile or project documentation
Run the migration generation command with a descriptive name
Review the generated migration SQL to ensure it matches your intent
Verify the migration can be applied cleanly (if possible, test on a temporary database)

metadata.task_description: In this repository, add an optional `nickname` field (text) to users. It should be stored and loaded like the other user fields and accepted by the Python client. Commit the change when it is ready to merge.
metadata.rationale: This trajectory encountered a commit failure because the repository required Conventional Commits format ('feat(users):' instead of 'Add optional'). The pre-commit hook revealed this requirement. Running 'make check' and 'make test' before committing would have also validated that generated code matched the schema and all tests passed.
metadata.trigger: Before making a git commit in an unfamiliar repository, especially after making code generation or schema changes
implementation_steps: Review the Makefile or project documentation for validation commands (check, test, lint)
Run all validation commands and ensure they pass
Attempt to commit; if rejected by a hook, read the error message carefully for format requirements
Check for .githooks/, .git/hooks/, or similar directories that may contain commit-msg or pre-commit hooks
Adjust commit message or code to meet requirements and retry
After successful commit, verify the commit log shows expected changes

metadata.task_description: In this repository, add an optional `nickname` field (text) to users. It should be stored and loaded like the other user fields and accepted by the Python client. Commit the change when it is ready to merge.
metadata.rationale: This trajectory efficiently discovered the implementation pattern by: 1) finding models.py to see current structure, 2) finding schema/models.yaml as the source of truth, 3) examining how store.py persists fields, 4) reviewing tests to see usage patterns. This systematic approach revealed that fields are defined in YAML, code is generated, and migrations are created separately.
metadata.trigger: When asked to add a new field or modify data structures in an unfamiliar codebase, especially one with code generation
implementation_steps: Find and examine the data model files (models.py, schema definitions) to see current structure
Look for schema source files (*.yaml, *.json, *.proto) that may be the source of truth
Read generation/build scripts to understand the code generation workflow
Examine persistence layer (store.py, database code) to understand how fields are saved/loaded
Review existing tests to see how fields are used in practice
Check for migration files to understand database evolution patterns

metadata.task_description: In this repository, add an optional `nickname` field (text) to users. It should be stored and loaded like the other user fields and accepted by the Python client. Commit the change when it is ready to merge.
metadata.rationale: This trajectory demonstrated thorough validation by creating temporary databases and testing: 1) user creation with nickname, 2) user creation without nickname (verifying it's optional), 3) updating nickname, 4) client payload validation with and without nickname. These tests caught potential issues before committing and confirmed the feature worked end-to-end.
metadata.trigger: After regenerating code from schema changes and before committing, especially when existing test suite doesn't cover the new field
implementation_steps: Write a temporary test script that creates instances with the new field set
Test creating instances without the new field to verify it's truly optional
Test persistence (insert) and retrieval (get) operations
Test update operations on the new field
Test client validation accepts the new field and still rejects invalid fields
Run the script and verify all operations succeed before committing
